analysis:
The only change is documentation in docs/operations/provider-release.md, head lines 196-198. It adds a statement that only pull-request runs can use Darkbloom Sandboxes (linked to developer/build.md#ci-runner-routing), and that master and dispatched runs always use the Blacksmith macOS-27 runners. The change touches no code, workflow, secret, signing, notarization, R2 or registration step. Release-integrity controls are unchanged: trusted-master resolution, signed-tag checks, the secret-free build and SDK qualification jobs, retained signed artifacts, and the registration/revocation fence. The threat model scopes these as trusted-repository-writer assumptions and covers provider artifact identity under T-034, T-054 and TB-011; none of that text is altered.

The new sentence is a claim about routing. The actual enforcement lives in workflow YAML and in the developer/build.md anchor, neither supplied here. I cannot verify that the described routing (PR-only sandboxes, master/dispatch pinned to Blacksmith) is implemented. If the workflows do not enforce it, a signing-adjacent job could run on a less-trusted runner. That is an unverified external contract, not evidence of a regression. A later pass should check the workflow runner selection and confirm that the signing, publication and cache-seeding jobs on master cannot be routed to Sandboxes. Also confirm the claim that PR caches do not seed master. No finding is raised.
